subject: Fastpath connector sandbox collaboration — Pinecone + S3 fallback
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Pinecone Integrations <integrations@pinecone.io>, Kevin Park <kevin@atlasdata.com>, sandbox-onboarding@acme.ai
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fastpath connector sandbox collaboration — Pinecone + S3 fallback

Hi team,

Thanks for the sync yesterday. To keep momentum, here are the concrete asks to stand up a short-lived sandbox so we can validate the "fastpath" connector pattern (LD: low-latency lookup against Pinecone with automatic S3 cold-tier fallthrough for older indices).

High-level scope:
- Pinecone: enable a sandbox project with a single replica and realtime index, sample index name pattern: redwood_fastpath_test_*
- Redwood: deploy a connector shim in our sandbox account that implements index discovery, health pings, and prefix-based routing.
- AtlasData: assist with sample rehydration flow and test vectors.

Kickoff asks:
1) Pinecone sandbox credentials (API key with project-scoped access)
2) S3 bucket ARN for fallthrough tests (we can use a temporary bucket; we only need read permissions)
3) A short mutual action plan (MAP) — I attached a draft spec with test vectors and success criteria.

Timeline proposal: 2-week sandbox window starting Mon 2028-05-15. Primary success criteria: sub-30ms lookup for hot keys, successful read-through to S3 for >99% of fallthrough attempts, and no connector-induced tokenization changes.

Marcus and Ben — can you take point on the connector deploy and instrumentation? Marcus, please include expected observability hooks (tracing/span tags, latency histogram). Ben, can you validate costs-per-call estimate for the sandbox?

Pinecone / Kevin — if that timeline works, send over the project key and any onboarding notes and we'll schedule a short kickoff.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Partner Integrations, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0139

From: Pinecone Integrations <integrations@pinecone.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kevin Park <kevin@atlasdata.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fastpath connector sandbox collaboration — Pinecone + S3 fallback

On Fri, May 11, 2028 at 09:12, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> High-level scope:
> - Pinecone: enable a sandbox project with a single replica and realtime index...

Thanks for the detailed plan, Karthik. We're aligned and can provision a sandbox project. Quick notes:
- We can provision the project and an API key today; API key will be scoped to the provided project name.
- Default index configuration: 1536-dim, HNSW, epsilon=0.1. If you need a different vector dim, tell us.
- For the fallthrough test, we'll allow a larger TTL on vectors so they expire into cold storage on your S3 bucket during the test window.

Action items from Pinecone:
- Provision project: pinecone-redwood-fastpath-2028 (we'll share key)
- Add a small demo dataset (10k vectors) and enable query logging for the sandbox project
- Provide a short-run cost estimate for the config above (attaching estimate)

We'll send the key by EOD. When your connector is wired, please run the sandbox test suite in the spec (fastpath-connector-spec-v1.pdf) and paste results in the shared Drive folder.

--
Pinecone Integrations Team
integrations@pinecone.io

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Pinecone Integrations <integrations@pinecone.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kevin Park <kevin@atlasdata.com>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fastpath connector sandbox collaboration — Pinecone + S3 fallback

Thanks, all — looks good. Quick engineering notes against the spec:
- We'll implement a two-stage lookup: 1) local sharded cache for the most recent prefixes (memory-backed LRU), 2) routed call to Pinecone for cold misses. If Pinecone returns a 404 for an index, we fall back to S3 rehydrate flow.
- Tracing: include span tags pinecone.index, pinecone.latency_ms, s3.read_fallback and connector.rehydrate_time_ms. We'll emit a metric connector.fallback.rate.
- Test vectors: the attached sandbox-test-vectors.csv includes 250 warm queries and 50 deep-cold queries to validate both paths.

Requested from Pinecone: can you enable query logging AND a per-query trace id passthrough so we can correlate spans (we'll add the header x-redwood-trace-id)?

Ben will run a quick cost sim and post in the Drive link. Assuming the tests pass, I'd like to cut a brief partner integration note we can share with Solutions to make the runtime behavior explicit for customers.

Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Platform Integrations
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Pinecone Integrations <integrations@pinecone.io>, Kevin Park <kevin@atlasdata.com>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fastpath connector sandbox collaboration — Pinecone + S3 fallback

Quick update after a cost pass and a small dry run in staging:
- Estimated incremental cost for a 2-week sandbox (10k vectors, single replica): ~ $420 for Pinecone usage + ~$15 for S3 GETs assuming 10k fallthrough reads.
- The connector's added CPU/memory is negligible for the small dataset. For production sizing we'd recommend a 10% buffer for peak QPS.
- I uploaded the cost sheet and raw run logs to the Drive folder.

Next steps I propose:
1) Pinecone shares API key + index name; Redwood will do an initial wiring and smoke test by Tue 2028-05-16.
2) Run the sandbox test vectors Wed 2028-05-17 through Thu 2028-05-18.
3) Collate metrics on Fri 2028-05-19 and decide on next steps (pilot vs broad enablement).

If Pinecone is OK with the above, we can start the provisioning.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Partner Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
